A Safe Path to Open Weights
items.summary: Abstract: Safe open-weight models are public goods, as they put AI development and safety work in many hands and make training choices inspectable. Open models also carry real misuse risks, and release is irreversible. To release safely, we must consider both the model and the ecosystem it enters. For the model, we conduct robust safety testing and research whether dangerous capabilities can be decoupled from general intelligence. For the ecosystem, we invest in its readiness through staged releases, supporting defenders, and collaboration with safety researchers. By iteratively choosing the most open option the evidence supports while building up the ecosystem's resilience, we can move toward openness safely. The mission of Thinking Machines is to build AI that extends human will and judgment. In pursuit of that mission, we recently released Inkling and Inkling-Small , two open-weight language models that anyone can own, run, and customize. Strong open-weight models put AI development in many hands. We believe that this is a good thing: the knowledge of what AI should do lives with the people doing the work, so they should be able to shape their models directly. All models, including our own, carry the assumptions and biases of those who trained it; open weights make those choices inspectable and revisable. Without strong open models, training and deployment expertise risks becoming concentrated in a few labs, leaving everyone else less able to understand, adapt, or govern the technology. items.title: Video generation models as world simulators
items.summary: We explore large-scale training of generative models on video data. Specifically, we train text-conditional diffusion models jointly on videos and images of variable durations, resolutions and aspect ratios. We leverage a transformer architecture that operates on spacetime patches of video and image latent codes. Our largest model, Sora, is capable of generating a minute of high fidelity video. Our results suggest that scaling video generation models is a promising path towards building general purpose simulators of the physical world.

items.title: Improving mathematical reasoning with process supervision
items.summary: We’ve trained a model to achieve a new state-of-the-art in mathematical problem solving by rewarding each correct step of reasoning (“process supervision”) instead of simply rewarding the correct final answer (“outcome supervision”). In addition to boosting performance relative to outcome supervision, process supervision also has an important alignment benefit: it directly trains the model to produce a chain-of-thought that is endorsed by humans.

items.title: Forecasting potential misuses of language models for disinformation campaigns and how to reduce risk
items.summary: OpenAI researchers collaborated with Georgetown University’s Center for Security and Emerging Technology and the Stanford Internet Observatory to investigate how large language models might be misused for disinformation purposes. The collaboration included an October 2021 workshop bringing together 30 disinformation researchers, machine learning experts, and policy analysts, and culminated in a co-authored report building on more than a year of research. This report outlines the threats that language models pose to the information environment if used to augment disinformation campaigns and introduces a framework for analyzing potential mitigations. Read the full report here.

items.title: Learning to play Minecraft with Video PreTraining
items.summary: We trained a neural network to play Minecraft by Video PreTraining (VPT) on a massive unlabeled video dataset of human Minecraft play, while using only a small amount of labeled contractor data. With fine-tuning, our model can learn to craft diamond tools, a task that usually takes proficient humans over 20 minutes (24,000 actions). Our model uses the native human interface of keypresses and mouse movements, making it quite general, and represents a step towards general computer-using agents.

items.title: Evolution through large models
AI-written critiques help humans notice flaws
items.summary: We trained “critique-writing” models to describe flaws in summaries. Human evaluators find flaws in summaries much more often when shown our model’s critiques. Larger models are better at self-critiquing, with scale improving critique-writing more than summary-writing. This shows promise for using AI systems to assist human supervision of AI systems on difficult tasks.

items.title: Techniques for training large neural networks

items.summary: We’ve discovered neurons in CLIP that respond to the same concept whether presented literally, symbolically, or conceptually. CLIP can be applied to any visual classification benchmark by simply providing the names of the visual categories to be recognized, similar to the “zero-shot” capabilities of GPT-2 and GPT-3.

items.title: Image GPT
items.summary: We find that, just as a large transformer model trained on language can generate coherent text, the same exact model trained on pixel sequences can generate coherent image completions and samples. By establishing a correlation between sample quality and image classification accuracy, we show that our best generative model also contains features competitive with top convolutional nets in the unsupervised setting.

items.title: Language models are few-shot learners
AI and efficiency
items.summary: We’re releasing an analysis showing that since 2012 the amount of compute needed to train a neural net to the same performance on ImageNet classification has been decreasing by a factor of 2 every 16 months. Compared to 2012, it now takes 44 times less compute to train a neural network to the level of AlexNet (by contrast, Moore’s Law would yield an 11x cost improvement over this period). Our results suggest that for AI tasks with high levels of recent investment, algorithmic progress has yielded more gains than classical hardware efficiency.

items.title: Jukebox
items.summary: We’re introducing Jukebox, a neural net that generates music, including rudimentary singing, as raw audio in a variety of genres and artist styles. We’re releasing the model weights and code, along with a tool to explore the generated samples.

items.title: Improving verifiability in AI development
items.summary: We’ve contributed to a multi-stakeholder report by 58 co-authors at 30 organizations, including the Centre for the Future of Intelligence, Mila, Schwartz Reisman Institute for Technology and Society, Center for Advanced Study in the Behavioral Sciences, and Center for Security and Emerging Technologies. This report describes 10 mechanisms to improve the verifiability of claims made about AI systems. Developers can use these tools to provide evidence that AI systems are safe, secure, fair, or privacy-preserving. Users, policymakers, and civil society can use these tools to evaluate AI development processes.

items.title: OpenAI Microscope
items.summary: We’re introducing OpenAI Microscope, a collection of visualizations of every significant layer and neuron of eight vision “model organisms” which are often studied in interpretability. Microscope makes it easier to analyze the features that form inside these neural networks, and we hope it will help the research community as we move towards understanding these complicated systems.

items.title: OpenAI standardizes on PyTorch
items.summary: We are standardizing OpenAI’s deep learning framework on PyTorch.

items.title: Scaling laws for neural language models
Dota 2 with large scale deep reinforcement learning
Deep double descent
items.summary: We show that the double descent phenomenon occurs in CNNs, ResNets, and transformers: performance first improves, then gets worse, and then improves again with increasing model size, data size, or training time. This effect is often avoided through careful regularization. While this behavior appears to be fairly universal, we don’t yet fully understand why it happens, and view further study of this phenomenon as an important research direction.

items.title: Procgen Benchmark

items.title: GPT-2: 1.5B release
items.summary: As the final model release of GPT-2’s staged release, we’re releasing the largest version (1.5B parameters) of GPT-2 along with code and model weights to facilitate detection of outputs of GPT-2 models. While there have been larger language models released since August, we’ve continued with our original staged release plan in order to provide the community with a test case of a full staged release process. We hope that this test case will be useful to developers of future powerful models, and we’re actively continuing the conversation with the AI community on responsible publication.

items.title: Solving Rubik’s Cube with a robot hand
items.summary: We’ve trained a pair of neural networks to solve the Rubik’s Cube with a human-like robot hand. The neural networks are trained entirely in simulation, using the same reinforcement learning code as OpenAI Five paired with a new technique called Automatic Domain Randomization (ADR). The system can handle situations it never saw during training, such as being prodded by a stuffed giraffe. This shows that reinforcement learning isn’t just a tool for virtual tasks, but can solve physical-world problems requiring unprecedented dexterity.

items.title: OpenAI Scholars 2020: Applications open

items.title: Fine-tuning GPT-2 from human preferences
items.summary: We’ve fine-tuned the 774M parameter GPT-2 language model using human feedback for various tasks, successfully matching the preferences of the external human labelers, though those preferences did not always match our own. Specifically, for summarization tasks the labelers preferred sentences copied wholesale from the input (we’d only asked them to ensure accuracy), so our models learned to copy. Summarization required 60k human labels; simpler tasks which continue text in various styles required only 5k. Our motivation is to move safety techniques closer to the general task of “machines talking to humans,” which we believe is key to extracting information about human values.

items.title: Emergent tool use from multi-agent interaction
items.summary: We’ve observed agents discovering progressively more complex tool use while playing a simple game of hide-and-seek. Through training in our new simulated hide-and-seek environment, agents build a series of six distinct strategies and counterstrategies, some of which we did not know our environment supported. The self-supervised emergent complexity in this simple environment further suggests that multi-agent co-adaptation may one day produce extremely complex and intelligent behavior.

items.title: Testing robustness against unforeseen adversaries
items.summary: We’ve developed a method to assess whether a neural network classifier can reliably defend against adversarial attacks not seen during training. Our method yields a new metric, UAR (Unforeseen Attack Robustness), which evaluates the robustness of a single model against an unanticipated attack, and highlights the need to measure performance across a more diverse range of unforeseen attacks.

items.title: GPT-2: 6-month follow-up
items.summary: We’re releasing the 774 million parameter GPT-2 language model after the release of our small 124M model in February, staged release of our medium 355M model in May, and subsequent research with partners and the AI community into the model’s potential for misuse and societal benefit. We’re also releasing an open-source legal agreement to make it easier for organizations to initiate model-sharing partnerships with each other, and are publishing a technical report about our experience in coordinating with the wider AI research community on publication norms.

items.title: Learning Day

items.title: Microsoft invests in and partners with OpenAI to support us building beneficial AGI
items.summary: Microsoft is investing $1 billion in OpenAI to support us building artificial general intelligence (AGI) with widely distributed economic benefits. We’re partnering to develop a hardware and software platform within Microsoft Azure which will scale to AGI. We’ll jointly develop new Azure AI supercomputing technologies, and Microsoft will become our exclusive cloud provider—so we’ll be working hard together to further extend Microsoft Azure’s capabilities in large-scale AI systems.

items.title: Why responsible AI development needs cooperation on safety
items.summary: We’ve written a policy research paper identifying four strategies that can be used today to improve the likelihood of long-term industry cooperation on safety norms in AI: communicating risks and benefits, technical collaboration, increased transparency, and incentivizing standards. Our analysis shows that industry cooperation on safety will be instrumental in ensuring that AI systems are safe and beneficial, but competitive pressures could lead to a collective action problem, potentially causing AI companies to under-invest in safety. We hope these strategies will encourage greater cooperation on the safe development of AI and lead to better global outcomes of AI.

items.title: Transfer of adversarial robustness between perturbation types
MuseNet
items.summary: We’ve created MuseNet, a deep neural network that can generate 4-minute musical compositions with 10 different instruments, and can combine styles from country to Mozart to the Beatles. MuseNet was not explicitly programmed with our understanding of music, but instead discovered patterns of harmony, rhythm, and style by learning to predict the next token in hundreds of thousands of MIDI files. MuseNet uses the same general-purpose unsupervised technology as GPT-2, a large-scale transformer model trained to predict the next token in a sequence, whether audio or text.

items.title: Generative modeling with sparse transformers
items.summary: We’ve developed the Sparse Transformer, a deep neural network which sets new records at predicting what comes next in a sequence—whether text, images, or sound. It uses an algorithmic improvement of the attention mechanism to extract patterns from sequences 30x longer than possible previously.

items.title: OpenAI Five defeats Dota 2 world champions
items.summary: OpenAI Five is the first AI to beat the world champions in an esports game, having won two back-to-back games versus the world champion Dota 2 team, OG, at Finals this weekend. Both OpenAI Five and DeepMind’s AlphaStar had previously beaten good pros privately but lost their live pro matches, making this also the first time an AI has beaten esports pros on livestream.

items.title: OpenAI Five Finals
items.summary: We’ll be holding our final live event for OpenAI Five at 11:30am PT on April 13.

items.title: Implicit generation and generalization methods for energy-based models
items.summary: We’ve made progress towards stable and scalable training of energy-based models (EBMs) resulting in better sample quality and generalization ability than existing models. Generation in EBMs spends more compute to continually refine its answers and doing so can generate samples competitive with GANs at low temperatures, while also having mode coverage guarantees of likelihood-based models. We hope these findings stimulate further research into this promising class of models.

items.title: OpenAI Scholars 2019: Meet our Scholars
items.summary: Our class of eight scholars (out of 550 applicants) brings together collective expertise in literature, philosophy, cell biology, statistics, economics, quantum physics, and business innovation.

items.title: OpenAI LP
items.summary: We’ve created OpenAI LP, a new “capped-profit” company that allows us to rapidly increase our investments in compute and talent while including checks and balances to actualize our mission.

items.title: Introducing Activation Atlases
items.summary: We’ve created activation atlases (in collaboration with Google researchers), a new technique for visualizing what interactions between neurons can represent. As AI systems are deployed in increasingly sensitive contexts, having a better understanding of their internal decision-making processes will let us identify weaknesses and investigate failures.

items.title: Neural MMO: A massively multiagent game environment
items.summary: We’re releasing a Neural MMO, a massively multiagent game environment for reinforcement learning agents. Our platform supports a large, variable number of agents within a persistent and open-ended task. The inclusion of many agents and species leads to better exploration, divergent niche formation, and greater overall competence.

items.title: Spinning Up in Deep RL: Workshop review
items.summary: On February 2, we held our first Spinning Up Workshop as part of our new education initiative at OpenAI.

items.title: AI safety needs social scientists
items.summary: We’ve written a paper arguing that long-term AI safety research needs social scientists to ensure AI alignment algorithms succeed when actual humans are involved. Properly aligning advanced AI systems with human values requires resolving many uncertainties related to the psychology of human rationality, emotion, and biases. The aim of this paper is to spark further collaboration between machine learning and social science researchers, and we plan to hire social scientists to work on this full time at OpenAI.

items.title: Better language models and their implications
items.summary: We’ve trained a large-scale unsupervised language model which generates coherent paragraphs of text, achieves state-of-the-art performance on many language modeling benchmarks, and performs rudimentary reading comprehension, machine translation, question answering, and summarization—all without task-specific training.

items.title: Computational limitations in robust classification and win-win results
OpenAI Fellows Summer 2018: Final projects
items.summary: Our first cohort of OpenAI Fellows has concluded, with each Fellow going from a machine learning beginner to core OpenAI contributor in the course of a 6-month apprenticeship.

items.title: How AI training scales
items.summary: We’ve discovered that the gradient noise scale, a simple statistical metric, predicts the parallelizability of neural network training on a wide range of tasks. Since complex tasks tend to have noisier gradients, increasingly large batch sizes are likely to become useful in the future, removing one potential limit to further growth of AI systems. More broadly, these results show that neural network training need not be considered a mysterious art, but can be rigorized and systematized.

items.title: Quantifying generalization in reinforcement learning
items.summary: We’re releasing CoinRun, a training environment which provides a metric for an agent’s ability to transfer its experience to novel situations and has already helped clarify a longstanding puzzle in reinforcement learning. CoinRun strikes a desirable balance in complexity: the environment is simpler than traditional platformer games like Sonic the Hedgehog but still poses a worthy generalization challenge for state of the art algorithms.

items.title: Spinning Up in Deep RL
items.summary: We’re releasing Spinning Up in Deep RL, an educational resource designed to let anyone learn to become a skilled practitioner in deep reinforcement learning. Spinning Up consists of crystal-clear examples of RL code, educational exercises, documentation, and tutorials.

items.title: Learning concepts with energy functions
items.summary: We’ve developed an energy-based model that can quickly learn to identify and generate instances of concepts, such as near, above, between, closest, and furthest, expressed as sets of 2d points. Our model learns these concepts after only five demonstrations. We also show cross-domain transfer: we use concepts learned in a 2d particle environment to solve tasks on a 3-dimensional physics-based robot.

items.title: Plan online, learn offline: Efficient learning and exploration via model-based control
Reinforcement learning with prediction-based rewards
items.summary: We’ve developed Random Network Distillation (RND), a prediction-based method for encouraging reinforcement learning agents to explore their environments through curiosity, which for the first time exceeds average human performance on Montezuma’s Revenge.

items.title: Learning complex goals with iterated amplification
items.summary: We’re proposing an AI safety technique called iterated amplification that lets us specify complicated behaviors and goals that are beyond human scale, by demonstrating how to decompose a task into simpler sub-tasks, rather than by providing labeled data or a reward function. Although this idea is in its very early stages and we have only completed experiments on simple toy algorithmic domains, we’ve decided to present it in its preliminary state because we think it could prove to be a scalable approach to AI safety.

items.title: Learning dexterity
items.summary: We’ve trained a human-like robot hand to manipulate physical objects with unprecedented dexterity.

items.title: Glow: Better reversible generative models
items.summary: We introduce Glow, a reversible generative model which uses invertible 1x1 convolutions. It extends previous work on reversible generative models and simplifies the architecture. Our model can generate realistic high resolution images, supports efficient sampling, and discovers features that can be used to manipulate attributes of data. We’re releasing code for the model and an online visualization tool so people can explore and build on these results.

items.title: Learning Montezuma’s Revenge from a single demonstration
items.summary: We’ve trained an agent to achieve a high score of 74,500 on Montezuma’s Revenge from a single human demonstration, better than any previously published result. Our algorithm is simple: the agent plays a sequence of games starting from carefully chosen states from the demonstration, and learns from them by optimizing the game score using PPO, the same reinforcement learning algorithm that underpins OpenAI Five.

items.title: OpenAI Five
items.summary: Our team of five neural networks, OpenAI Five, has started to defeat amateur human teams at Dota 2.

items.title: Retro Contest: Results
items.summary: The first run of our Retro Contest—exploring the development of algorithms that can generalize from previous experience—is now complete.

items.title: Learning policy representations in multiagent systems
Improving language understanding with unsupervised learning
items.summary: We’ve obtained state-of-the-art results on a suite of diverse language tasks with a scalable, task-agnostic system, which we’re also releasing. Our approach is a combination of two existing ideas: transformers and unsupervised pre-training. These results provide a convincing example that pairing supervised learning methods with unsupervised pre-training works very well; this is an idea that many have explored in the past, and we hope our result motivates further research into applying this idea on larger and more diverse datasets.

items.title: Gym Retro
items.summary: We’re releasing the full version of Gym Retro, a platform for reinforcement learning research on games. This brings our publicly-released game count from around 70 Atari games and 30 Sega games to over 1,000 games across a variety of backing emulators. We’re also releasing the tool we use to add new games to the platform.

items.title: AI and compute
items.summary: We’re releasing an analysis showing that since 2012, the amount of compute used in the largest AI training runs has been increasing exponentially with a 3.4-month doubling time (by comparison, Moore’s Law had a 2-year doubling period)[^footnote-correction]. Since 2012, this metric has grown by more than 300,000x (a 2-year doubling period would yield only a 7x increase). Improvements in compute have been a key component of AI progress, so as long as this trend continues, it’s worth preparing for the implications of systems far outside today’s capabilities.

items.title: AI safety via debate
items.summary: We’re proposing an AI safety technique which trains agents to debate topics with one another, using a human to judge who wins.

items.title: Evolved Policy Gradients
items.summary: We’re releasing an experimental metalearning approach called Evolved Policy Gradients, a method that evolves the loss function of learning agents, which can enable fast training on novel tasks. Agents trained with EPG can succeed at basic tasks at test time that were outside their training regime, like learning to navigate to an object on a different side of the room from where it was placed during training.

items.title: Gotta Learn Fast: A new benchmark for generalization in RL
Retro Contest

items.title: Improving GANs using optimal transport
On first-order meta-learning algorithms
Reptile: A scalable meta-learning algorithm
items.summary: We’ve developed a simple meta-learning algorithm called Reptile which works by repeatedly sampling a task, performing stochastic gradient descent on it, and updating the initial parameters towards the final parameters learned on that task. Reptile is the application of the Shortest Descent algorithm to the meta-learning setting, and is mathematically similar to first-order MAML (which is a version of the well-known MAML algorithm) that only needs black-box access to an optimizer such as SGD or Adam, with similar computational efficiency and performance.

items.title: OpenAI Scholars
items.summary: We’re providing 6–10 stipends and mentorship to individuals from underrepresented groups to study deep learning full-time for 3 months and open-source a project.

items.title: Some considerations on learning to explore via meta-reinforcement learning
Ingredients for robotics research
items.summary: We’re releasing eight simulated robotics environments and a Baselines implementation of Hindsight Experience Replay, all developed for our research over the past year. We’ve used these environments to train models which work on physical robots. We’re also releasing a set of requests for robotics research.

items.title: Multi-Goal Reinforcement Learning: Challenging robotics environments and request for research

items.summary: Come to OpenAI’s office in San Francisco’s Mission District for talks and a hackathon on Saturday, March 3rd.

items.title: OpenAI supporters
items.summary: We’re excited to welcome new donors to OpenAI.

items.title: Preparing for malicious uses of AI
items.summary: We’ve co-authored a paper that forecasts how malicious actors could misuse AI technology, and potential ways we can prevent and mitigate these threats. This paper is the outcome of almost a year of sustained work with our colleagues at the Future of Humanity Institute, the Centre for the Study of Existential Risk, the Center for a New American Security, the Electronic Frontier Foundation, and others.

items.title: Interpretable machine learning through teaching
items.summary: We’ve designed a method that encourages AIs to teach each other with examples that also make sense to humans. Our approach automatically selects the most informative examples to teach a concept—for instance, the best images to describe the concept of dogs—and experimentally we found our approach to be effective at teaching both AIs

items.title: Discovering types for entity disambiguation
items.summary: We’ve built a system for automatically figuring out which object is meant by a word by having a neural network decide if the word belongs to each of about 100 automatically-discovered “types” (non-exclusive categories).

items.title: Requests for Research 2.0
items.summary: We’re releasing a new batch of seven unsolved problems which have come up in the course of our research at OpenAI.

items.title: Scaling Kubernetes to 2,500 nodes
Block-sparse GPU kernels
items.summary: We’re releasing highly-optimized GPU kernels for an underexplored class of neural network architectures: networks with block-sparse weights. Depending on the chosen sparsity, these kernels can run orders of magnitude faster than cuBLAS or cuSPARSE. We’ve used them to attain state-of-the-art results in text sentiment analysis and generative modeling of text and images.

items.title: Learning sparse neural networks through L₀ regularization
Interpretable and pedagogical examples
Learning a hierarchy
items.summary: We’ve developed a hierarchical reinforcement learning algorithm that learns high-level actions useful for solving a range of tasks, allowing fast solving of tasks requiring thousands of timesteps. Our algorithm, when applied to a set of navigation problems, discovers a set of high-level actions for walking and crawling in different directions, which enables the agent to master new navigation tasks quickly.

items.title: Generalizing from simulation
items.summary: Our latest robotics techniques allow robot controllers, trained entirely in simulation and deployed on physical robots, to react to unplanned changes in the environment as they solve simple tasks. That is, we’ve used these techniques to build closed-loop systems rather than open-loop ones as before.

items.title: Sim-to-real transfer of robotic control with dynamics randomization
Asymmetric actor critic for image-based robot learning
Domain randomization and generative models for robotic grasping
Competitive self-play
items.summary: We’ve found that self-play allows simulated AIs to discover physical skills like tackling, ducking, faking, kicking, catching, and diving for the ball, without explicitly designing an environment with these skills in mind. Self-play ensures that the environment is always the right difficulty for an AI to improve. Taken alongside our Dota 2 self-play results, we have increasing confidence that self-play will be a core part of powerful AI systems in the future.

items.title: Meta-learning for wrestling
items.summary: We show that for the task of simulated robot wrestling, a meta-learning agent can learn to quickly defeat a stronger non-meta-learning agent, and also show that the meta-learning agent can adapt to physical malfunction.

items.title: Nonlinear computation in deep linear networks
Learning to model other minds
items.summary: We’re releasing an algorithm which accounts for the fact that other agents are learning too, and discovers self-interested yet collaborative strategies like tit-for-tat in the iterated prisoner’s dilemma. This algorithm, Learning with Opponent-Learning Awareness (LOLA), is a small step towards agents that model other minds.

items.title: Learning with opponent-learning awareness
OpenAI Baselines: ACKTR & A2C
items.summary: We’re releasing two new OpenAI Baselines implementations: ACKTR and A2C. A2C is a synchronous, deterministic variant of Asynchronous Advantage Actor Critic (A3C) which we’ve found gives equal performance. ACKTR is a more sample-efficient reinforcement learning algorithm than TRPO and A2C, and requires only slightly more computation than A2C per update.

items.title: More on Dota 2
items.summary: Our Dota 2 result shows that self-play can catapult the performance of machine learning systems from far below human level to superhuman, given sufficient compute. In the span of a month, our system went from barely matching a high-ranked player to beating the top pros and has continued to improve since then. Supervised deep learning systems can only be as good as their training datasets, but in self-play systems, the available data improves automatically as the agent gets better.

items.title: Dota 2
items.summary: We’ve created a bot which beats the world’s top professionals at 1v1 matches of Dota 2 under standard tournament rules. The bot learned the game from scratch by self-play, and does not use imitation learning or tree search. This is a step towards building AI systems which accomplish well-defined goals in messy, complicated situations involving real humans.

items.title: Gathering human feedback
items.summary: RL-Teacher is an open-source implementation of our interface to train AIs via occasional human feedback rather than hand-crafted reward functions. The underlying technique was developed as a step towards safe AI systems, but also applies to reinforcement learning problems with rewards that are hard to specify.

items.title: Better exploration with parameter noise
items.summary: We’ve found that adding adaptive noise to the parameters of reinforcement learning algorithms frequently boosts performance. This exploration method is simple to implement and very rarely decreases performance, so it’s worth trying on any problem.

items.title: Proximal Policy Optimization
items.summary: We’re releasing a new class of reinforcement learning algorithms, Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO), which perform comparably or better than state-of-the-art approaches while being much simpler to implement and tune. PPO has become the default reinforcement learning algorithm at OpenAI because of its ease of use and good performance.

items.title: Robust adversarial inputs
items.summary: We’ve created images that reliably fool neural network classifiers when viewed from varied scales and perspectives. This challenges a claim from last week that self-driving cars would be hard to trick maliciously since they capture images from multiple scales, angles, perspectives, and the like.

items.title: Hindsight Experience Replay
Teacher–student curriculum learning
Faster physics in Python
items.summary: We’re open-sourcing a high-performance Python library for robotic simulation using the MuJoCo engine, developed over our past year of robotics research.

items.title: Learning from human preferences
items.summary: One step towards building safe AI systems is to remove the need for humans to write goal functions, since using a simple proxy for a complex goal, or getting the complex goal a bit wrong, can lead to undesirable and even dangerous behavior. In collaboration with DeepMind’s safety team, we’ve developed an algorithm which can infer what humans want by being told which of two proposed behaviors is better.

items.title: Learning to cooperate, compete, and communicate
items.summary: Multiagent environments where agents compete for resources are stepping stones on the path to AGI. Multiagent environments have two useful properties: first, there is a natural curriculum—the difficulty of the environment is determined by the skill of your competitors (and if you’re competing against clones of yourself, the environment exactly matches your skill level). Second, a multiagent environment has no stable equilibrium: no matter how smart an agent is, there’s always pressure to get smarter. These environments have a very different feel from traditional environments, and it’ll take a lot more research before we become good at them.

items.title: UCB exploration via Q-ensembles

items.title: Spam detection in the physical world

items.title: Evolution strategies as a scalable alternative to reinforcement learning
items.summary: We’ve discovered that evolution strategies (ES), an optimization technique that’s been known for decades, rivals the performance of standard reinforcement learning (RL) techniques on modern RL benchmarks (e.g. Atari/MuJoCo), while overcoming many of RL’s inconveniences.

items.title: More than just code review
items.summary: The key skill required to make productive use of coding agents is being able to confidently instruct them on how to make changes and then confidently verify that those changes have been applied in the correct way. Sometimes this involves reviewing every line of code they have written, but there are other ways to achieve that goal. Eyeballing every line of code has never been the most effective way to validate a change to a piece of software. Tags: code-review , coding-agents , generative-ai , agentic-engineering , ai , llms

items.title: llm 0.33
items.summary: Release: llm 0.33 My highlights from this release: Upgraded to the OpenAI Python library 3.x and switched the HTTP client dependency from httpx to httpx2 . #1608 , #1631 I shipped a quick 0.32.1 fix for this yesterday, but this is the more comprehensive fix. llm embed and llm embed-multi now accept --key . The Python EmbeddingModel.embed() , EmbeddingModel.embed_multi() , Collection.embed() and Collection.embed_multi() methods accept key= too, passing the resolved per-call key to embedding plugins without changing shared model state. Existing plugins that read self.key continue to work through a compatibility fallback. Thanks, ChrisJr404 . #757 , #1620 The embedding models now use the same pattern for keys that regular LLM models do. llm prompt -t/--template can now be repeated to combine templates in order. This allows model configuration and options from one template to be used with a prompt from another. This unlocks a neat pattern where you can create templates that package a model with a set of default options: llm -m gpt-5.6-luna -o reasoning_effort high --save lhigh llm "Generate an SVG of a pelican riding a bicycle" --save pelican # Combine and run the templates llm -t lhigh -t pelican Reasoning-capable Responses API models now support a reasoning_summary option with auto , concise , and detailed values. This can be used with llm openai endpoint --responses . #1600 This is particularly useful for exercising different models that provide their own imitation of the OpenAI Responses API. Tags: annotated-release-notes , llm

items.title: Quoting Linus Torvalds
items.summary: And this was a debug session from hell, enormously helped by an AI doing much of the grunt-work. I'd like to call it my tireless helper, but the AI several times stated flat out that this was impossible and unsolvable and that we should just write a report about it. I suspect those things have been trained by people who may not be quite as stubborn as I am. But while the AI was ready to give up several times, it did keep adding debug code and analyzing it faithfully when I pushed. So credit where credit is due and I let the AI write the commit message above. — Linus Torvalds , drm/xe: Don't hand out the flat CCS storage as usable VRAM Tags: linus-torvalds , linux , generative-ai , ai-assisted-programming , ai , llms

items.title: Anthropic’s best AI model struggles to attract users as cheaper tools thrive
items.summary: Anthropic’s best AI model struggles to attract users as cheaper tools thrive A few interesting numbers in this FT story gathered from "people with knowledge of the matter": Anthropic's "annualized revenue" for July is up to $65bn - it was $47bn in May, and I collected more historic numbers here . Anthropic expect Q3 to be profitable according to the same model they used to declare Q2 profitable. "It also told investors that it had 6,000 customers that spend $100,000 annually or more." As for OpenAI, "annualised revenue has jumped 35 per cent in the quarter to date and is now over $40bn, with the launch of GPT 5.6 in July jolting the company’s performance after a sluggish start to the year". This article also introduced me to the Ramp AI index , which uses billing data from 70,000 Ramp credit card using companies to estimate model adoption. Here's Ramp's breakdown of Anthropic model spend for July 2026, which looks reasonable given that Opus 5 was only released on July 24th, and supports the idea that Fable's cost has made it a less popular model: Opus 4.8: 28.0% Sonnet 4.6: 8.3% Fable 5: 8.0% Opus 4.6: 6.9% Sonnet 5: 3.6% Opus 5: 3.5% Opus 4.7: 1.7% Sonnet 4.5: 1.3% Haiku 4.5: 1.0% Opus 4.5: 0.7% Via Hacker News Tags: ai , openai , generative-ai , llms , anthropic , claude , claude-mythos-fable

items.title: Quoting Drew Breunig
items.summary: Prior to Fable, it felt silly to waste too much time improving your coding harness or context strategies. A new model would arrive at the same price (or cheaper!) and paper over most of your problems. But then Fable landed. It was (and still is!) incredible . But the cost was so high and Opus was good enough (as was 5.6, K3, and even GLM) for most of the code we needed. So we started to think about what work went where. — Drew Breunig , Fable & The End of the Free Lunch Tags: drew-breunig , anthropic , claude , llm-pricing , ai , llms , generative-ai , claude-mythos-fable

items.title: Your executable is a SQLite database
items.summary: Your executable is a SQLite database Farid Zakaria describes a neat Linux pattern for creating a SQLite database file that can be directly used as an executable binary. The trick sets the SQLite file format's 4-byte application ID (68 bytes into the file) to SELF, standing for Structured Executable & Linkable Format. The various components of the ELF executable format are then arranged into a number of different SQLite tables, using this schema . Their self-exec interpreter ( C code here ) can then extract and execute the necessary pieces. You can additionally use a Linux mechanism called binfmt_misc to teach the kernel to execute that any time it encounters an executable matching that binary pattern. Farid uses NixOS here, but without NixOS I think registration looks something like this: printf '%s\n' ':self:M:68:SELF::/usr/local/bin/self-exec:' \ > /proc/sys/fs/binfmt_misc/register Via Hacker News Tags: c , linux , sqlite

items.title: EVE Online: The Move to Python 3 Begins!
items.summary: EVE Online: The Move to Python 3 Begins! EVE Online has been one of the most interesting case studies in Python at scale for over twenty years now. They've been running on Stackless Python since their launch in 2003, and their last major upgrade was 16 years ago, to Stackless Python 2.7 in 2010 . Their upgrade to Python 3 will start using the futurize script against 2.4 million lines of code, followed by careful manual review of the ~20,000 places where Python 2 and 3 behavior differ - for example 1 / 2 is 0 in Python 2 but is 0.5 in Python 3. There's nothing in this announcement about how they plan to replace Stackless, but at their conference last year they presented Scheduling in Carbon: Leaving Stackless Python Behind describing how they replaced Stackless in the Carbon engine for their more recent game EVE Frontier, using their (now open source) carbonengine/scheduler library. Via Lobster.rs Tags: eve-online , migrations , python , python3 , stackless

items.title: Quoting Paul Dix
items.summary: The fact that AI wrote 1M LOC and then refined it over the course of the next couple of months to produce a reliable piece of software that is currently running on millions of developer machines is absolutely mind blowing. And you can say, “well it’s not that impressive because they had an oracle to compare against, so it was simple to go from one language to another”, but I think that’s selling this entire thing short. If you can build a verification system and give proper direction, AI can produce a highly complex, highly sophisticated piece of software and it can continue to refine it until it just works. — Paul Dix , The end of programming Tags: coding-agents , ai-assisted-programming , generative-ai , bun , ai , llms

items.summary: 内华达州拉斯维加斯的 AWS 本地区域现已全面推出。这一新的 AWS 本地区域支持 Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud（Amazon EC2）C7i、M7i、R7i 和 C8gn 实例、Amazon Elastic Block Store（Amazon EBS）卷类型 gp3、gp2、io1、sc1 和 st1，以及 Amazon Elastic Container Service（Amazon ECS）、Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service（Amazon EKS）、应用程序负载均衡器和 AWS Direct Connect。 AWS Local Zones 是 AWS 基础设施部署，可扩展计算、存储、联网等核心服务以及其他精选服务，使其更贴近全球各都市区域。AWS Local Zones 可助您为最终用户工作负载实现个位数毫秒级延迟，满足数据驻留要求，支持人工智能/机器学习推理工作负载，并加速遗留应用程序向云端的迁移与现代化，同时保持与 AWS 区域一致的 AWS API、工具和服务。AWS Local Zones 已在全球 30 多个都市区域推出。 要开始使用，请在 AWS Global View（AWS 全局视图）的 Regions and Zones （区域和可用区）选项卡中启用拉斯维加斯本地区域（us-west-2-las-2a），或者使用 ModifyAvailabilityZoneGroup API 进行启用。如需了解定价信息，请访问 AWS Local Zones 定价页面 。 要了解更多信息，请访问 AWS Local Zones 概览页面 。

items.title: 适用于 InfluxDB 的 Amazon Timestream 现已支持客户自主管理型密钥
items.summary: 适用于 InfluxDB 的 Amazon Timestream 现已支持使用 AWS Key Management Service（AWS KMS）客户自主管理型密钥，来加密 InfluxDB 2 数据库实例、InfluxDB 2 只读副本和 InfluxDB 3 集群中的静态数据。在创建数据库资源时，客户可选择对称 AWS KMS 密钥。 适用于 InfluxDB 的 Timestream 使用选定密钥对 InfluxDB 2 和 InfluxDB 3 资源的底层数据库存储进行加密。密钥必须与数据库资源位于同一个 AWS 账户和 AWS 区域中。客户需在资源创建期间指定密钥。创建资源后将无法更改密钥。 客户自主管理型密钥支持通过 AWS 管理控制台、AWS 命令行界面（AWS CLI）和适用于 InfluxDB 的 Timestream 应用程序编程接口（API）提供。此功能已在提供适用于 InfluxDB 的 Timestream 的所有 AWS 区域推出。使用客户自主管理型密钥不会产生适用于 InfluxDB 的 Timestream 的额外费用。您需要支付标准 AWS KMS 费用。 对客户自主管理型密钥的支持已在提供适用于 InfluxDB 的 Amazon Timestream 的所有 AWS 区域 推出。要开始使用，请打开 Amazon Timestream 控制台。有关更多信息，请参阅 适用于 InfluxDB 的 Amazon Timestream 文档 和 定价页面 。

Breaking Claude Code Opus 5 Auto Mode
items.summary: Breaking Claude Code Opus 5 Auto Mode Anthropic are putting a great deal of faith in Claude Code's auto mode for protecting their coding agent users against prompt injection attacks. They recently made that the default and have made bold claims about its effectiveness. Johann Rehberger is one of the most credible prompt injection researchers active today. He found an attack against auto mode which he claims works 80% of the time, by tricking Claude Code into downloading and uncompressing a zip archive, then executing code that imports base64 without noticing that this will import and execute a local struct.py file extracted from the archive. In a few cases auto mode directly prevented the agent from preventing harmful code from continuing to execute! In a few runs Claude tried to terminate the malware process once it noticed the compromise, but Auto Mode denied the cleanup command. Claude detects the compromise, but Auto Mode blocks its cleanup command The safety mechanism itself can become part of the failure. The classifier allowed the creation of the malware process, but then it blocked the command intended to stop it! I agree with Johann's conclusion here: the only safe way to run agents if there's any risk of attracting the attention of an adversarial attack is with a sandbox: Run unattended coding agents in a container, VM or OS sandbox. Restrict network egress. Monitor your agents. Do not expose home directories, SSH keys, cloud credentials,… to the agent runtime. items.title: Amazon Connect Customer 现已支持经理与其数据对话
items.summary: Amazon Connect Customer 现已支持经理使用自然语言与数据对话，数秒内即可获取答案、对应的支撑依据以及解决方案。经理一直都拥有这些数据，但他们没有充足时间去梳理仪表板，找出绩效驱动因素并确定后续行动。现在，Amazon Connect Customer 可以为其完成这些工作。此功能可在涵盖自助服务、座席绩效与队列性能的 150 多项指标中进行搜索，找出关键问题、解释原因，并给出最优的后续行动建议。 经理可以从宏观提问切入，再在同一对话中向下深挖细节。例如，经理可以询问哪些队列最适合实施自动化，Amazon Connect Customer 随即核查处理时长与事后处理工作最高的队列，随后返回一份按优先级排序的队列清单，包含置信度评分与预期影响。以往需要分析师、仪表板以及数周调研工作才能完成的任务，如今在数秒内即可生成一个按优先级排序的行动计划。 此功能已在支持 Amazon Connect Customer 人工智能代理的所有 AWS 区域推出。要了解更多信息，请访问我们的 产品文档 。

items.title: AWS Deadline Cloud 现可在 Deadline Cloud 监控器中跟踪自动下载状态
items.summary: AWS Deadline Cloud 监控器现可显示从云端运行的作业中自动下载文件的进度、状态和运行状况。Deadline Cloud 是一项完全托管式服务，可帮助团队在云端运行计算密集型工作负载，适用于视觉效果、动画、产品设计、仿真和游戏开发。客户可通过 Deadline Cloud 监控器（DCM）桌面应用程序查看其渲染环境、作业、资源和成本。现在，客户还可以使用该监控器来确认自动配置的作业输出已成功下载到目标驱动器。 通过此次更新，监控器应用程序分别在作业与任务级别新增一个“下载状态”列，其中显示下载进度并确认所有输出文件已保存到您的驱动器上。该列旁会显示一个标识，用于表明状态的时效性。如果文件因任何原因不可用，该应用程序将提供清晰的后续步骤指引。此举无需再手动对驱动器进行验证，帮助团队在下游任务开始前稳妥确认输出是否可用。在大规模渲染管道中，手动检查文件并不现实，该功能在此场景下价值尤为突出。 要了解有关 AWS Deadline Cloud 和 Deadline Cloud 监控器桌面应用程序中新的自动下载状态功能的更多信息，请访问 https://aws.amazon.com/deadline-cloud/。

items.title: 适用于 Argo CD 的 Amazon EKS 功能现已支持自定义配置
items.summary: 适用于 Argo CD 的 Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service（Amazon EKS）功能现已支持通过集群中的标准 argocd-cm ConfigMap 进行自定义配置。此功能可为您提供完全托管式 GitOps 持续交付体验，您现在可以对其进行调优以适配团队的工作方式。您可以为自定义资源定义自定义运行状况检查、定制 Argo CD UI 横幅内容、调整该功能监听并对比其所管理资源的方式等。您可以像在上游 Argo CD 中那样配置这些设置，AWS 会将其应用于您的托管功能。 通过此次发布，集群管理员现在可以对 Argo CD 报告应用程序运行状况的方式进行更精细的控制。默认情况下，Argo CD 未针对自定义资源提供内置的运行状况逻辑，因此，应用程序可能在其资源仍处于预置状态时报告为运行正常，同步波次也可能在这些资源准备就绪前向前推进。通过自定义运行状况检查，您可以自行定义此逻辑。例如，数据库资源的运行状况检查可让应用程序保持在处理中状态，直到数据库准备就绪。此功能还包括针对 AWS Controllers for Kubernetes（ACK）和 KRO（Kube 资源编排工具）资源的内置运行状况检查，因此，它们无需额外配置即可报告准确的运行状况。 您可以在提供适用于 Argo CD 的 EKS 功能的所有 AWS 区域配置该功能。要了解更多信息，请参阅 Amazon EKS 和《Amazon EKS 用户指南》中的 配置 Argo CD 设置 。

items.title: AWS Glue 6.0 降价 30%，并支持 Iceberg v3
items.summary: AWS Glue 6.0 现已全面推出，降价 30%，并且完全支持 Apache Iceberg v3、更新版本的 Apache Hudi 和 Delta Lake，新增功能可助力提高开发人员工作效率。AWS Glue 6.0 还将运行时升级到 Apache Spark 4.1、Python 3.13 和 Scala 2.13。 借助 Apache Iceberg v3，AWS Glue 6.0 新增带自动拆解能力的 VARIANT 数据类型（用于更快读取半结构化数据）、删除向量（用于高性能行级更新）、geometry 和 geography 数据类型（用于空间处理），以及通过 UNKNOWN 数据类型和 DEFAULT 列值实现的灵活模式演进。Glue 6.0 还推出了多项提高开发人员工作效率与性能的功能，例如，可消除重复编排代码的 Spark 声明式管道、可实现亚秒级延迟的实时模式流处理，以及优化 PySpark 性能的 Arrow 原生 Python UDF。借助这些功能，您可以使用 AWS Glue 实施大规模 ETL、定期批处理工作负载、流分析和 AI 应用程序开发。 AWS Glue 6.0 已在所有 AWS 商业区域、AWS GovCloud（美国）和 AWS 中国区域推出。 要开始使用，请在创建新作业时，从 AWS Glue 控制台或 SageMaker 融通式合作开发工作室的版本下拉列表中选择 Glue 6.0，或者使用 AWS Glue 中 Apache Spark 的生成式人工智能升级代理 迁移现有作业。要了解更多信息，请参阅 AWS Glue 文档 和 AWS Glue 定价 。

items.title: Amazon SES 现已支持打开追踪与点击追踪覆盖参数
items.summary: Amazon Simple Email Service（SES）现已支持 SendEmail API 和 SendBulkEmail API 中的打开追踪与点击追踪覆盖参数。发件人可以在单次 API 调用中启用或禁用打开追踪与点击追踪，而不是通过单独的配置集来管理追踪首选项。 以前，要控制追踪行为，需要为打开追踪与点击追踪设置的每种组合分别维护一个独立的配置集。利用这项新功能，您可以直接在发送请求中指定追踪首选项，降低配置开销，并简化遵从收件人级追踪许可的处理流程。这对于必须遵从每位收件人许可选择的发件人尤为实用，有助于满足 GDPR 和 CNIL 指引等数据保护要求。 追踪覆盖参数按单次请求应用，其优先级高于关联配置集中定义的追踪行为。您无需更改现有配置集结构，即可实现精细控制。使用此功能不会产生额外费用。 此功能已在提供 Amazon SES 的所有 AWS 区域推出。 要了解更多信息，请参阅 Amazon SES 开发人员指南 中有关打开追踪与点击追踪的文档。

items.title: Amazon EC2 C8gd 实例、M8gd 实例和 R8gd 实例现已在更多 AWS 区域推出
items.summary: 具有高达 11.4 TB 基于 NVMe 的本地 SSD 块级存储的 Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud（Amazon EC2）C8gd、M8gd 和 R8gd 实例现已在更多区域推出。C8gd 实例现已在亚太地区（新加坡）推出，M8gd 实例现已在墨西哥（中部）和亚太地区（墨尔本）推出，R8gd 实例现已在欧洲（苏黎世）推出。这些实例由 AWS Graviton4 处理器提供支持，相比基于 Graviton3 的实例，其性能提高多达 30%。与基于 AWS Graviton3 的同类实例相比，它们在 I/O 密集型数据库工作负载方面的性能提升高达 40%，在 I/O 密集型实时数据分析场景中，查询速度提升高达 20%。这些实例基于 AWS Nitro System 构建，非常适合需要访问高速、低延迟本地存储的应用程序。 每个实例有 12 种不同的大小可供选择。这种实例可提供高达 50Gbps 的网络带宽和高达 40Gbps 的 Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) 带宽。此外，客户现在可以使用 EC2 实例带宽权重配置将这些实例的网络和 Amazon EBS 带宽调整 25%，以便更灵活地分配带宽资源，从而更好地优化工作负载。这些实例就 24xlarge、48xlarge、metal-24xl 和 metal-48xl 大小提供 Elastic Fabric Adapter (EFA) 网络。 C8gd 实例非常适合计算密集型工作负载，例如高性能 Web 服务器、批处理、分布式分析、广告投放、视频编码和游戏服务器。M8gd 实例非常适合处理均衡的工作负载，包括应用服务器、微服务、企业应用程序以及中小型数据库。R8gd 实例适用于内存密集型工作负载，例如内存数据库、实时大数据分析、大型内存缓存以及科学计算应用程序。 要了解更多信息，请参阅 Amazon C8gd 实例 、 Amazon M8gd 实例 和 Amazon R8gd 实例 。要了解如何将工作负载迁移到基于 Graviton 的实例，请参阅 AWS Graviton Fast Start 迅速开启程序计划 和 Porting Advisor for Graviton 。要开始使用，请参阅 AWS 管理控制台 。

items.title: Amazon ECS 现在可以自动检测和修复代理连接受损的容器实例
items.summary: Amazon Elastic Container Service （Amazon ECS）现在可以自动检测和修复容器实例，使客户无需手动干预，即可减少未检测到的工作负载故障，并提高应用程序可用性。 通过此次发布，Amazon ECS 将持续监控跨容器实例的代理连接。基础设施事件（如 EBS 卷性能下降、主机过热事件或网络连接故障）可能会切断 ECS 代理与 ECS 控制面板的连接。Amazon ECS 现在为所有计算选项引入了一类新的容器实例运行状况变更事件（AGENT_CONNECTIVITY）：AWS Fargate、Amazon ECS 托管实例和 Amazon ECS on EC2。对于 ECS 托管实例和 AWS Fargate，ECS 会自动执行恢复操作，即自动停止正在运行的任务并启动替换容量，同时注销受损实例。在 Amazon ECS on EC2 上运行工作负载的客户，可以使用此运行状况变更事件来加速实例更换工作流程。 此功能已在所有 AWS 商业区域和 AWS GovCloud（美国） 区域 推出，无需额外付费。要了解更多信息，请参阅 监控 Amazon ECS 容器实例运行状况 。

items.title: SageMaker MLflow 现在支持客户自主管理型密钥
items.summary: SageMaker MLflow 现在支持客户通过 AWS Key Management Service（KMS），使用客户自主管理型密钥（CMK）对数据进行加密。 这一增强功能使具有严格的安全性与合规性要求的组织能够自行管理加密密钥。借助客户自主管理型密钥，您可以通过与 AWS CloudTrail 的集成获得更强大的安全控制能力和全面的审计功能。您可以使用自己的 KMS 密钥对数据进行加密，并跟踪所有数据访问以进行安全审计。 客户自主管理型密钥必须在您的 MLflow App 所属的 AWS 账户和区域中创建，且仅支持对称的 AWS KMS 密钥。 此功能已在 提供 MLflow App 的所有 AWS 区域全面推出。要了解更多信息，请访问 SageMaker MLflow 详细信息页面 。

items.title: Amazon EKS 现在支持每个集群关联多个外部 OIDC 身份提供者
items.summary: Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service（Amazon EKS）现在支持每个集群关联多个外部 OpenID Connect（OIDC）身份提供者。您最多可以将 10 个 OIDC 身份提供者关联到一个集群，这样您就可以更灵活地对要访问 Kubernetes 集群的用户和工作负载进行身份验证。 许多组织为不同的用户群体（如员工、承包商和 CI/CD 系统）使用不同的身份提供者。现在，您可以将每个提供者直接关联到您的集群，而无需将用户整合到单个提供者中，也无需运行中间身份凭证代理程序。每个提供者都独立配置和管理，因此每个群体通过自己的提供者和身份映射进行身份验证。您现有的 IAM 身份验证将继续与所有配置的提供者一起运作。您可以像以前一样，使用 AWS 管理控制台或通过 AWS CLI 和 AWS SDK 使用 AssociateIdentityProviderConfig API 添加每个提供者。 此功能已在提供 Amazon EKS 的所有 AWS 区域推出，无需额外付费。要了解更多信息，请参阅《Amazon EKS 用户指南》中的 通过外部 OIDC 提供者向用户授予 Kubernetes 访问权限 。

items.title: Amazon Aurora 现在支持 PostgreSQL 18.4、17.10、16.14、15.18 和 14.23
items.summary: Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL 兼容版现在支持 PostgreSQL 版本 18.4、17.10、16.14、15.18 和 14.23，这些版本包含来自 PostgreSQL 社区的错误修复以及特定于 Aurora 的增强功能。建议您升级到最新的次要版本，以修复已知的常见漏洞和泄露（CVE）并享受这些改进带来的好处，详情请参阅这些 发行说明 。 您可以使用自动次要版本升级在计划维护时段内升级数据库。要大规模简化操作，请启用自动次要版本升级，并使用 AWS Organizations 升级部署策略 分阶段编排多次升级，先在低优先级环境中完成验证，然后再升级最重要的环境。有关更多信息，请参阅 升级 Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL 数据库集群 。 Amazon Aurora 设计具有全球规模的高性能和可用性，与 PostgreSQL 完全兼容。它提供可缩减至零的无服务器计算、支持多区域韧性的 Aurora Global Database、用于提升 I/O 密集型工作负载性价比的 Aurora I/O 优化版，以及内置的安全功能和持续备份。要开始使用，请查看我们的 入门页面 。

items.title: Amazon SageMaker HyperPod 增强了对 Ray 的支持
items.summary: Amazon SageMaker HyperPod 现已增强对 Ray 的支持，提供内置的可观测性、弹性训练、加速推理和托管式开发环境。Ray 是一种常见的开源框架，用于在统一的计算层上扩展 AI 工作负载，涵盖数据处理、分布式训练、强化学习和模型服务。在生产规模下于 Kubernetes 上运行 Ray 可能带来运维负担：作业挂起、静态团队分配导致 GPU 利用率低下，以及多步骤的可观测性设置。此外，缺乏交互式开发环境意味着每项代码更改都需要再次提交作业并熟悉 kubectl。 HyperPod 现在为 Ray 带来了更简便的开发、弹性训练和加速推理。数据科学家可以在 Amazon SageMaker Studio 中通过 Web 界面创建、编辑、监控和删除 Ray 集群，然后将 JupyterLab、代码编辑器或本地 IDE 附加到正在运行的 Ray 集群，以集群规模的计算能力进行交互式迭代。多节点 Ray 集群的行为类似于本地开发环境，因此您可以立即测试每项更改，无需等待新作业排队和启动。在可观测性方面，HyperPod 预置了显示 Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus 指标的 Grafana 控制面板，并允许通过安全的浏览器链接一键访问 Ray 控制面板，让您从首次运行即可查看工作负载的运行状况。在大规模训练方面，HyperPod 的节点自动恢复和挂起作业检测功能可处理 GPU 故障、作业挂起、损失峰值和吞吐量下降等问题。分层检查点可从集群内存恢复状态以最大限度地提高产出，而任务治理则通过配额、优先级和抢占来提高计算利用率。它们共同确保您的长时间训练在失败中持续进行，并最大化每 GPU 小时的有效工作量。对于 Ray Serve 推理，分层 KV 缓存通过重复使用缓存的前缀来缩短获得首个令牌的时间，并且您可以直接部署 Amazon SageMaker JumpStart 模型。 开源 Ray 代码无需更改即可运行，您既可以采用 SageMaker Studio 中专门构建的体验，也可以将各项功能单独集成到您自己的 ML 平台中。 在支持 SageMaker HyperPod 的 AWS 区域中，由 Amazon EKS 编排的 HyperPod 集群均可获得 Ray 支持。要了解更多信息，请参阅 SageMaker HyperPod 文档 ，并浏览 交互式演示 。

items.title: Amazon Connect Customer 现在支持对座席语音和聊天对话进行信息提取
items.summary: Amazon Connect Customer 现在支持信息提取，可自动从语音和聊天互动中捕获关键数据，从而减少手动数据捕获工作，提高座席和主管的工作效率。信息提取可捕获账号、预订 ID 和产品名称等明文值，以及从对话中推断出来的衍生见解，例如联系原因、提供的解决方案和承诺采取的后续措施。 您可以定义对话分析规则，指定提取哪些内容以及何时提取。提取针对的是原始联系内容，发生在脱敏之前，因此您可以捕获特定的数据点，同时仍能隐去录音和转录中的敏感值。座席可以在联系后工作期间查看提取的值，主管可以使用这些值来搜索和查看联系，开发人员可以通过 API、Kinesis 数据流和 S3 输出文件以编程方式访问这些值。您还可以将提取的值直接输入到电子邮件通知、任务创建和案例创建等规则操作中，将非结构化对话转变为自动化体验。例如，旅游公司可以自动从互动中提取“酒店名称”、“预订 ID”和“致电原因”，然后将其填入出站电子邮件并创建后续任务，从而消除手动数据输入并缩短处理时间。 要了解更多信息，请参阅《Amazon Connect Customer 管理员指南》中的 信息提取 ，或访问 Amazon Connect Customer 网站 。有关按 AWS 区域提供的对话分析功能的完整列表，请参阅 各区域的 Connect Customer 功能可用性 。

items.title: AWS ParallelCluster 3.16 新增节点内诊断工具
items.summary: AWS ParallelCluster 3.16 现已全面推出，新增节点内诊断工具、集群稳定性改进以及更新的 HPC 和 AI/ML 软件堆栈。 pcluster-diag 是一款内置于 ParallelCluster AMI 中的诊断工具，让您能够通过单个命令对任何集群节点运行诊断检查，并获取结构化报告，从而更轻松地识别问题。此版本还通过更具弹性的集群创建、更新和映像构建，强化了集群生命周期。软件堆栈已刷新，更新了 NVIDIA 驱动程序、CUDA、EFA 安装程序和 Slurm 版本。要开始使用 pcluster-diag，请参阅 使用 pcluster-diag 进行故障排除 。有关更多详细信息，请查看 AWS ParallelCluster 3.16.0 发行说明 。 AWS ParallelCluster 是一种开源集群管理工具，可让研发客户及其 IT 管理员在 AWS 上运行高性能计算（HPC）集群。ParallelCluster 旨在以安全方式自动将云资源预置为可弹性扩展的 HPC 集群，以便在 AWS 上大规模运行科学和工程工作负载。ParallelCluster 现已在 此处 列出的 AWS 区域免费提供，您只需为运行应用程序所需的 AWS 资源付费。 有关在 AWS 上启动 HPC 集群的更多信息，请访问 ParallelCluster 用户指南 。要开始使用 ParallelCluster，请参阅 ParallelCluster UI 和 CLI 的安装说明。

items.title: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Terra 和 Luna 现已在 AWS GovCloud（美国）的 Amazon Bedrock 上推出
items.summary: GPT-5.6 Terra 和 Luna 现已在 AWS GovCloud（美国西部）和 AWS GovCloud（美国东部）的 Amazon Bedrock 上全面推出，将 OpenAI 中一系列最智能的模型引入 Bedrock 的新一代推理引擎，该引擎旨在实现高性能以及出色的安全性和可靠性。GPT-5.6 在智能和效率方面树立了新的标杆，使您能够在更短的时间内解决更棘手的问题，并且每个 Token 更加智能。这两个模型跨越了从平衡性能（Terra）到快速、成本高效的推理（Luna）的能力层级。 使用 GPT-5.6，您可以构建自主编程代理、执行长期基因组学与生物学分析，以及开展更深入的网络安全研究。Terra 以一半的成本提供 GPT-5.5 级别的性能，而 Luna 则以最低价格提供快速、高性价比的推理。GPT-5.6 还支持带显式缓存断点的提示缓存，这使得代理工作流程中的重复上下文可按 90% 的折扣计费，并且不会随着规模扩大而累积增加成本。 GPT-5.6 Terra 和 Luna 在 Amazon Bedrock 上支持 100 万个令牌的上下文窗口，使您能够在单个请求中处理完整的代码库、长篇文档和多回合代理对话历史记录。模型可基于更大范围上下文开展推理，返回更准确连贯的响应，无需分块处理，且不会发生信息丢失。 有关区域可用性，请参阅 Amazon Bedrock 区域可用性页面 。 要开始使用 Terra 和 Luna，请访问 Amazon Bedrock 控制台 或 bedrock-mantle 端点上的 Responses API。要了解更多信息，请参阅 Amazon Bedrock 文档 和 发布博客文章 。

items.title: Amazon RDS for MySQL 现在支持新的次要版本 8.4.11
items.summary: 即日起， Amazon Relational Database Service（Amazon RDS）for MySQL 支持 MySQL 次要版本 8.4.11，这是 MySQL 社区发布的最新次要版本。除了操作方面的改进外，MySQL 8.4.11 还引入了对后量子 TLS（PQ-TLS）密钥交换的支持，为您提供了用于加密传输中数据的后量子密码学选项。建议您升级到更新的次要版本，以修复早期 MySQL 版本中的 CVE，并享受漏洞修复、性能改进及 MySQL 社区增加的新功能带来的好处。有关 RDS for MySQL 8.4.11 中增强功能的更多信息，请参阅 Amazon RDS 用户指南 和 MySQL 8.4.11 发行说明。 您可以利用自动次要版本升级，在计划的维护时段自动将数据库升级到更新的次要版本。您还可以利用 Amazon RDS 托管式蓝绿部署 对 MySQL 实例进行更安全、更简单的更新。要了解有关升级数据库实例的更多信息（包括自动升级次要版本和蓝绿部署），请参阅 Amazon RDS 用户指南 。 Amazon RDS for MySQL 让用户能够在云中轻松设置、操作和扩展 MySQL 部署。有关定价详细信息和区域可用性，请参阅 Amazon RDS for MySQL 。在 Amazon RDS 管理控制台 中创建或更新完全托管式 Amazon RDS for MySQL 数据库。

items.title: AWS Neuron 2.32 为 Trn2 和 Trn 引入了扩展的 NKI 编程、MXFP8 训练内核和可变大小的集合通信
items.summary: AWS Neuron 2.32.0 现已推出，引入了 NKI 0.6.0，包含设备内 Top-K 指令，为等级包含不同大小张量的内核提供可变长度的 all-gather 集合通信，以及用于数据依赖迭代的新循环构造。 此版本还引入了 13 个新的 NKI Library 内核，用于混合专家（MoE）训练和稀疏注意力，以及一项新的 Neuron 代理式开发技能，可将转换器模型移植到 vLLM Neuron 插件。NKI Library 内核涵盖 DeepSeek-V3.2 稀疏多头潜在注意力的上下文编码、用于解码步骤的 MXFP8 注意力，以及一个匹配的 MXFP8 前向和后向传递，使块级 MoE 层能够在 MXFP8 中进行端到端训练，同时还为 22 个额外内核提供 PyTorch 参考实现。 Neuron Runtime 在 Trn2 和 Trn3 上增加了可变大小的 all-gather、reduce-scatter 和 all-to-all 集合通信，让每个等级都能贡献或接收不同数量的元素。vLLM Neuron 插件已升级至 vLLM 0.24.0，并包含在所有 Neuron 深度学习 AMI 和深度学习容器中。Neuron Compiler 增加了对 64 位整数编译的显式控制，而 Neuron Explorer 则在系统跟踪视图中增加了每核主机的 CPU 利用率。 AWS Neuron 已在提供 Amazon EC2 Trn1、Trn2、Trn3、Inf2 和 Inf1 实例的所有 AWS 区域推出。有关区域可用性的更多信息，请参阅 AWS 区域表 。 要开始使用，请参阅以下资源： AWS Neuron 2.32.0 发行说明 Neuron Kernel 接口（NKI）文档 Neuron Agentic Development AWS Neuron

items.title: Amazon Bedrock 宣布降低 OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol 的定价
items.summary: 今天，OpenAI 宣布将下调 GPT-5.6 Sol 的 API 价格。继近期 Terra 和 Luna 的价格下调之后，Sol 现价降至每百万个输入令牌 4 美元，每百万个输出令牌 20 美元，这相当于输入定价降低了 20%，输出定价降低了 33.3%。此促销定价将至少持续至 2026 年 11 月 21 日。 无论您是构建自主编程代理、运行复杂的多步骤分析，还是执行高级研究工作流程，更低的定价都为您提供了更多空间来试验和扩展已有的有效方案。GPT-5.6 Sol 在代理式编程基准测试中表现出色，且价格更低，使其更适用于持续的高容量工作负载。 有关 GPT-5.6 Sol 的最新区域可用性，请查看 AWS 区域 页面。要了解更多信息并查看定价，请参阅有关 GPT-5.6 Sol 的 Amazon Bedrock 文档 。

items.title: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore 内存现已支持从非对话 JSON 有效载荷中提取记忆
items.summary: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore 内存现已接受 CreateEvent API 上的 JSON 有效载荷类型，因此代理可以从结构化数据和多回合对话中提取和整合长期记忆。开发人员可以将行为事件、活动日志、系统事件和其他 JSON 数据（每个有效载荷最多 100 KB）直接传递到提取管道中。无需先将其重塑为合成对话消息。 提取管道处理 JSON 有效载荷的方式与处理对话相同，利用所有四种提取策略生成长期记忆：语义、用户偏好、摘要和情景。 非对话 JSON 有效载荷摄取功能现已在支持 AgentCore 内存的所有区域推出，与现有功能完全兼容。要开始使用，只需将 JSON 有效载荷添加到您的 事件 中即可。

items.title: Amazon Redshift 现在支持并发扩展来自 Amazon Kinesis Data Streams 的流式摄取工作负载
items.summary: Amazon Redshift 自 补丁 P203 起支持并发扩展，以刷新与 Amazon Kinesis Data Streams（KDS）连接的流式实体化视图（MV）。 Amazon Web Services（AWS）Redshift 流式摄取支持以低延迟高速将数据从 Amazon KDS 摄取到 Amazon Redshift 数据仓库。数据采用 Redshift 流式实体化视图，提供对外部数据的快速访问，缩短了数据访问时间，并降低了存储成本。用户可以使用 SQL 命令，为其 Amazon Redshift 集群或 Redshift Serverless 工作组配置流式摄取。设置完成后，每次流式实体化视图刷新每秒都能摄取数百兆字节的数据。如果您启用了并发扩展，您的流式工作负载现在将自动扩展，即释放主 Amazon Redshift 集群或工作组，以运行其他更高优先级的工作负载。 您可以立即开始在提供 Amazon Redshift 的所有 AWS 区域使用这项新功能来扩展您的工作负载，并使用可预测的服务水平协议来构建弹性分析应用程序。要开始使用，请参阅 Amazon Redshift 文档 的 并发扩展 、 实体化视图 和 流式摄取 部分。

Just a rumour of a bug is enough to find a security exploit these days
items.summary: Just a rumour of a bug is enough to find a security exploit these days Anil Madhavapeddy is a professor of computer science at Cambridge and a core maintainer of the OCaml compiler. In this somewhat alarming post he reports that security issues in OCaml projects are seeing evidence of attempted exploits within minutes of patches being shared for discussion: This normally takes a few days and a release within a week or two is reasonable. Within about ten minutes (!) this website was fielding probes for percent-encoded traversal sequences, indicating that automated watchers are keeping an eye on public repositories. Modern coding agents have become so effective at finding flaws that the slightest hint at a new bug can be enough information for them to find it, something Anil has been able to demonstrate using his own agents, switching to DeepSeek V4 Pro⁠ when Claude Fable refused the task. Anil points out that this rate of discovery appears incompatible with existing open source embargo practices for new issues. If an issue can become an exploit this fast, we need to figure out new processes for keeping our communities safe. rclone maintainer Nick Craig-Wood confirms in the Hacker News comments that his project is seeing this problem: In the first 10 years of the rclone project we received about 20 security disclosures through GitHub. We had to deal with over 40 in the last month! That has taken a huge amount of my time, even using AI tools to triage and come up with fixes for review. The hit rate for those security disclosures is pretty good - about 75% of them have a nugget

items.title: AWS IoT Core 现已支持适用于时间序列数据的原生 InfluxDB 路由
items.summary: AWS IoT Core 现已支持 InfluxDB 规则操作 ，将时间序列数据从您的物联网（IoT）设备直接路由至 InfluxDB 数据库，无需编写自定义设备端代码或使用中间云服务。AWS IoT Core 是一项完全托管式服务，可将数十亿台 IoT 设备安全地连接到 AWS 云，并将 IoT 设备数据路由至 AWS 和第三方服务。 新的 InfluxDB 规则操作会自动将设备中的时间序列数据转换为 InfluxDB 的行协议格式，并将其写入由 Amazon Timestream 托管或自托管的 InfluxDB 集群。新的规则操作还支持以下两种批处理模式，助力您优化成本和吞吐量：设备端批处理，允许设备向 AWS IoT Core 发送预批处理的有效载荷；服务器端批处理，允许 IoT 规则引擎在对 InfluxDB 进行写入之前对多条消息进行聚合。例如，生命科学公司能够以毫秒级粒度批量采集来自科学仪器的数千条遥测数据，并直接将其写入 InfluxDB 进行监控，而无需构建自定义数据管道。 要开始使用，请将您的 IoT 设备连接到 AWS IoT Core，并定义一个 InfluxDB 规则操作，以便指定目标数据库以及身份验证和批处理参数。InfluxDB 规则操作已在提供适用于 InfluxDB 的 Amazon Timestream 的所有 AWS 全球区域推出。要了解更多信息，请访问 AWS IoT Core 开发人员指南 。

items.title: AWS Batch 现已支持 Amazon ECS 托管实例
items.summary: AWS Batch 现已支持 Amazon ECS 托管实例（ECS MI）作为新的计算选项，使您能够在 AWS 托管的基础设施上运行 GPU 加速型和计算密集型批处理工作负载。借助 AWS Batch on ECS MI，您现在可以访问 GPU 加速型实例，AWS 会自动处理 AMI 更新、安全补丁和实例生命周期，从而消除客户管理的 Amazon EC2 基础设施的运营开销。 要开始使用，请使用 AWS Batch CreateComputeEnvironment API 或 AWS Batch 管理控制台创建 AWS Batch on ECS MI 计算环境。您可以在 managedInstancesProvider 块中指定允许的实例类型和联网配置，将计算环境与作业队列关联，并使用按需型容量、竞价型容量或预留容量提交作业。 提供 AWS Batch 的所有 AWS 区域 都支持 AWS Batch on ECS 托管实例。有关更多信息，请参阅 AWS Batch 用户指南 。

items.title: 容量预留资源组现已支持 Amazon EC2 容量块和可中断容量预留
items.summary: 即日起，您可以将适用于 ML 的 Amazon EC2 容量块和可中断容量预留添加到容量预留资源组中。Amazon EC2 提供不同的预留服务，例如，按需容量预留（ODCR）、可中断容量预留和适用于 ML 的容量块。以前，容量预留资源组只能包含 ODCR。现在，您可以将任意类型的容量预留添加到容量预留资源组，从而更轻松地在整个预留容量组合中启动 EC2 实例。 要使用此功能，请创建一个容量预留资源组，向其添加任何容量预留，然后在启动请求中将该组设为目标。在使用 EC2 实例集和 EC2 自动扩缩组时，您还可以跨预留类型指定优先级首选项，并配置为在预留容量耗尽时自动回退至 EC2 按需型容量。 使用此功能不会产生额外费用。此功能已在支持适用于 ML 的容量块和可中断 ODCR 的所有 AWS 区域推出，但 AWS GovCloud（美国）和中国区域除外。 要开始使用，请参阅 容量预留资源组 和 容量预留用户指南 。

items.title: AWS Lambda MicroVMs 现已支持 AWS PrivateLink
items.summary: AWS Lambda MicroVMs 现已支持 AWS PrivateLink，允许直接从 Amazon Virtual Private Cloud（VPC）资源与 Lambda MicroVMs 建立私有连接，而无需将流量暴露至公共互联网。通过此次发布，金融服务、医疗保健和政府企业的受监管工作负载可在使用 Lambda MicroVMs 进行构建时，满足严格的网络隔离要求。 PrivateLink VPC 端点提供从您的 VPC 到 AWS 服务的私有连接，确保在与 AWS 服务进行通信时，流量无需流经公共互联网。通过今天的发布，此功能已扩展至 Lambda MicroVMs。需要与 Lambda MicroVMs 的私有连接的开发人员和 IT 团队，现在可以在其 VPC 中创建 PrivateLink VPC 端点，来调用 MicroVM API（例如，创建 MicroVM 镜像或启动 MicroVMs）并连接到每个 MicroVM 的 HTTP 端点。 可使用 AWS 管理控制台、AWS CLI、AWS CloudFormation 或 AWS SDK 创建 Lambda MicroVMs 的 PrivateLink VPC 端点。提供 Lambda MicroVMs 的所有区域都支持此功能。要了解最新的区域可用性，请访问 按区域探索 AWS 功能页面 。 要了解有关结合使用 PrivateLink 与 Lambda MicroVMs 的更多信息，请参阅 开发人员指南 。 有关定价详情，请参阅 AWS PrivateLink 定价 。要了解有关为 AWS 服务配置私有连接的更多信息，请访问 AWS PrivateLink 开发人员指南 。

items.title: Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL 支持次要版本 18.6、17.11、16.15、15.19 和 14.24
items.summary: Amazon Relational Database Service（RDS）for PostgreSQL 现已支持最新的次要版本 18.6、17.11、16.15、15.19 和 14.24。我们建议您升级到最新的次要版本，以修复早期 PostgreSQL 版本中的通用漏洞披露（CVE），并利用 PostgreSQL 社区提供的错误修复和改进。 您可以使用自动次要版本升级在计划维护时段内升级数据库。要大规模简化操作，请启用自动次要版本升级，并使用 AWS Organizations 升级部署策略 分阶段编排多次升级，先在低优先级环境中完成验证，然后再升级最重要的环境。您还可以使用 Amazon RDS 蓝绿部署最大限度地缩短次要版本升级的停机时间。有关更多信息，请参阅 升级 RDS for PostgreSQL 数据库引擎 。 Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL 让您能够在云中轻松设置、运行和扩展 PostgreSQL 部署。有关定价详细信息和区域可用性，请参阅 Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL 定价 。在 Amazon RDS 管理控制台 中或使用 AWS 命令行界面（CLI）创建或更新完全托管式 Amazon RDS 数据库。

items.title: Amazon Connect Customer 现已支持更新案例的客户资料或在案例创建后添加客户资料
items.summary: Amazon Connect Customer 现已支持座席更改案例的客户资料或在案例创建后选择客户资料。如果案例与错误的客户关联，座席可以更新客户资料，保障案例历史记录准确。如果在创建案例时未能识别客户（例如，共享号码来电、需身份核验等场景），座席还可以后续添加客户资料。 Amazon Connect Cases 已在以下 AWS 区域推出：美国东部（弗吉尼亚州北部）、美国西部（俄勒冈州）、加拿大（中部）、欧洲地区（法兰克福）、欧洲地区（伦敦）、亚太地区（首尔）、亚太地区（新加坡）、亚太地区（悉尼）、亚太地区（东京）和非洲（开普敦）。要了解更多信息并开始使用，请访问 Amazon Connect Cases 网页 和 文档 。

items.title: IAM Roles Anywhere 现已提供适用于 AWS SDK 的 Java 插件
items.summary: AWS Identity and Access Management（IAM）Roles Anywhere 现已提供面向 适用于 Java 的 AWS SDK v2 的插件，使得在 AWS 外部运行的工作负载能够直接从 Java 应用程序进程中获取临时 AWS 凭证。该插件在与您的应用程序相同的 Java 虚拟机（JVM）中运行，无需将 IAM Roles Anywhere 凭证助手作为单独的进程运行，也无需在 AWS 配置文件中配置 credential_process。 您可以在适用于 Java 的 AWS SDK v2 服务客户端生成器上配置该插件，以自动解析临时凭证，而无需编写凭证提取逻辑。该插件负责调用 CreateSession，并在凭证到期前自动刷新凭证。它支持 RSA、椭圆曲线（EC）和 ML-DSA 密钥类型，并且要求使用 Java 8 或更高版本。使用该插件无需支付额外费用。 IAM Roles Anywhere 已在所有 AWS 区域 推出，包括 AWS GovCloud（美国）区域、AWS European Sovereign Cloud（德国）区域和中国区域。要开始使用该 Java 插件，请参阅 IAM Roles Anywhere Java 插件文档 。有关当前版本、发行说明和签名验证说明，请参阅 Maven Central 网站上的 插件页面 和 GitHub 上的 roles-anywhere-java 存储库 。

items.title: AWS Lambda 推出支持 Node.js 26 和 Python 3.15 的托管运行时公共预览版
items.summary: 今日，AWS Lambda 推出托管运行时公共预览，首批支持 Node.js 26 与 Python 3.15。这使客户、合作伙伴和上游语言社区能够在托管运行时正式版本（GA）发布之前试用即将推出的版本，并与 Lambda 团队分享反馈。 以前，Lambda 托管运行时直接以正式版本推出。由于运行时一经发布即可供生产工作负载使用，因此在正式版本推出后，Lambda 团队无法实施可能影响现有函数的更改。公共预览版的托管运行时使您能够在正式版本推出之前测试工作负载并报告问题，此阶段我们仍可能进行破坏性变更，以便及时响应您的反馈进行调整。第三方可观测性提供商、基础设施即代码工具和部署框架也能在正式版本推出前获得充足时间来验证兼容性。由于公共预览版的托管运行时可能会在预览期间出现破坏性变更，因此它们不在 Lambda SLA 或 AWS Technical Support 计划的涵盖范围内，且不得用于生产工作负载。公共预览版的托管运行时使用与最终的正式版运行时相同的运行时标识符，因此，当运行时的正式版本推出后，您的函数会自动完成过渡，无需执行任何操作。 要开始使用，请从 Lambda 控制台的运行时下拉列表中选择“Node.js 26（预览版）”或“Python 3.15（预览版）”，或者在 AWS CLI、CloudFormation、AWS SAM 或 AWS CDK 中指定 nodejs26.x 或 python3.15 作为运行时标识符。 公共预览版的 Node.js 26 和 Python 3.15 托管运行时已在所有 AWS 商业区域、AWS GovCloud（美国）区域和中国区域推出。使用预览版运行时的函数采用标准 Lambda 费率，无需额外付费。 要了解更多信息，请参阅我们的 博客文章 。要分享反馈，请访问 Node.js 26 和 Python 3.15 的专用 GitHub 问题页面。

items.title: Amazon RDS 现已支持 Microsoft SQL Server 的最新 CU
items.summary: Amazon Relational Database Service（Amazon RDS）for SQL Server 现已支持 Microsoft SQL Server 的最新累积更新（CU）。此版本包括对 Microsoft SQL Server 2025 CU6 KB5093421 （RDS 版本 17.00.4055.5.v1）的支持。 有关这些更新中包含的改进和修复的更多信息，请参阅 Microsoft 关于 KB5093421 的文档。我们建议您使用 Amazon RDS 管理控制台、AWS SDK 或 CLI 升级 Amazon RDS for SQL Server 实例以应用这些更新。您可以在 Amazon RDS SQL Server 用户指南中关于升级 RDS Microsoft SQL Server 数据库引擎的部分 详细了解如何升级数据库实例。

items.title: Amazon RDS for Oracle 现已支持 2026 年 7 月版本更新
items.summary: Amazon Relational Database Service（Amazon RDS）for Oracle 现已支持面向 Oracle Database 版本 19c、21c 和 26ai 的 Oracle 2026 年 7 月版本更新 （RU）。我们建议升级到 2026 年 7 月 RU，因为它包含针对 Oracle 数据库产品的安全更新。 从 2026 年 7 月版开始，Oracle Database 19c 中 RU 的命名格式更改为 <version>.ru-<YYYY-MM>.mrp-<YYYY-MM>.r<N>。例如，面向 Oracle Database 19c 的 RDS for Oracle 2026 年 7 月版季度 RU 名为 19.0.0.0.ru-2026-07.mrp-2026-07.r1。当 Oracle 发布面向 Oracle Database 19c 和 26ai 的月度关键安全补丁更新（CSPU）时，Amazon RDS 将以 MRP 版本的形式提供该更新，MRP 会把 CSPU 与 Oracle 推荐的其他修复程序一并打包。Oracle Database 21c RU 保留其现有的命名格式。有关详细信息，请参阅 版本更新和月度推荐补丁 。 您可以通过 Amazon RDS 管理控制台或使用 AWS SDK 或 CLI 应用 2026 年 7 月 RU。要在维护时段内自动对数据库实例应用更新，请启用“自动次要版本升级”功能。 您还可以使用 AWS Organizations 升级部署策略，错开 Amazon RDS 数据库实例的次要版本自动升级。借助这项功能，您可以自动将更新应用到非生产环境，验证更新，然后自动将相同的更新应用到生产环境。有关使用 AWS Organizations 升级部署策略进行次要版本自动升级的更多详细信息，请参阅 Amazon RDS for Oracle 文档 。

items.title: AWS Secrets Manager 新增对 Cisco Security Platform 和 Netskope 的托管式外部密钥支持
items.summary: AWS Secrets Manager 现已扩展其托管式外部密钥功能以包含 Cisco Security Platform API 密钥和 Netskope API 令牌，使您能够直接从 AWS 管理控制台自动轮换这些第三方凭证，而无需编写任何自定义轮换代码。 对于 Cisco Security Platform（Security Cloud Control），AWS Secrets Manager 会按您的计划自动轮换 API 密钥的刷新令牌，使凭证始终保持有效，并捕获 Cisco 定期重新颁发的新的刷新令牌。遵循 Cisco 的标准 OAuth 模式，您的应用程序可按需将存储的刷新令牌交换为短期访问令牌。对于 Netskope，Secrets Manager 通过 Netskope 的 SCIM API 轮换 RBACv3 服务账户 REST API 令牌，并在轮换完成之前验证新生成的令牌。这两种集成均具备自认证能力，即存储的凭证可自行授权完成轮换，因此无需额外提供管理员凭证。 这两项新增集成被纳入托管式外部密钥现有支持范围，现已支持的对象包括 BigID、Confluent Cloud、Datadog、GitLab、Jenkins、MongoDB Atlas、Okta、Paddle、Salesforce、Snowflake 和 SonarQube。 Cisco Security Platform 和 Netskope 托管式外部密钥已在支持 AWS Secrets Manager 托管式外部密钥的所有 AWS 区域推出。要了解更多信息，请访问 AWS Secrets Manager 托管式外部密钥文档 。

items.title: AWS Lambda 函数现已支持完整的 IAM 基于资源的策略
items.summary: AWS Lambda 函数现已支持完整的 Identity and Access Management（IAM） 基于资源的策略 ，使平台管理员和安全团队能够使用 AWS IAM 的全部功能来定义精细访问权限。借助完整的 IAM 基于资源的策略，您可以在单个策略文档中为多个主体和操作定义权限，并利用所有 IAM 条件键 。 以前，Lambda 函数要求客户为每个主体单独添加权限。对于需要大规模管理权限的平台管理员和安全团队而言，该模式的灵活性有限。 现在，Lambda 函数支持完整的 IAM 基于资源的策略，包括所有 IAM 条件键。这为运营多账户架构或管理多项资源的团队提供了更丰富的策略能力，并简化了策略管理工作。例如，您现在可以使用 IAM 条件键，基于源 IP 或主体标签限制访问权限；平台团队现在可允许多项服务使用单个策略调用一个函数，而不是维护多条语句来添加权限。 您可以使用 AWS Lambda 控制台中的 JSON 编辑器、AWS CLI、AWS SDK 或基础设施即代码工具（例如 AWS CloudFormation 和 AWS SAM），一次性更新基于资源的策略。要了解更多信息，请浏览《AWS Lambda 开发人员指南》中的 Lambda 基于资源的策略示例 。 完整的 IAM 基于资源的策略已在所有 AWS 商业区域 推出，不额外收取费用。

items.title: MSK 复制器现已支持 OAuth 2.0（SASL/OAUTHBEARER）身份验证，用于执行从外部 Apache Kafka 集群到 Amazon MSK 的复制操作
items.summary: Amazon MSK 复制器现已支持 OAuth 2.0（SASL/OAUTHBEARER）身份验证，用于将数据从外部 Apache Kafka 集群（包括本地集群、AWS 上自管理的集群或其他云提供商）复制到 Amazon MSK 预置集群 。借助此功能，配置了 OAuth/OIDC 身份验证的外部 Apache Kafka 集群，现在可以使用 MSK 复制器将工作负载迁移到 Amazon MSK，使用基于 MSK 的集群作为失效转移或备份目标来支持灾难恢复，并实现跨混合和多云环境分发数据。 MSK 复制器是 Amazon MSK 的一项功能，可自动在 Kafka 集群之间复制数据，而无需管理自定义复制基础设施或配置开源工具。以前，MSK 复制器支持 SASL/SCRAM 和 mTLS 身份验证，用于连接到外部 Apache Kafka 集群。通过此次发布，您现在还可以结合使用 OAuth 2.0 身份验证与 MSK 复制器，将数据从外部 Kafka 集群复制到 Amazon MSK。与自管理的复制工具不同，MSK 复制器允许您在复制期间保留原始 Kafka 主题名称，同时自动避免无限的复制循环。它还可以双向同步使用者组偏移，使您能够按任何顺序在集群之间独立移动生产者和使用者，而不会出现协调限制或数据丢失的风险。 提供 MSK 复制器的所有 AWS 区域都支持这项新功能。要了解更多信息，请参阅 MSK 复制器 文档 、 产品页面 、 定价页面 和此 AWS 博客文章 。

items.summary: Introducing Hy4 Preview New open weight text input (no vision) LLM from Chinese company Tencent today: 770B total parameters, 49B active parameters, 1M token context window, 1.56TB on Hugging Face . This is a big size increase from their previous Hy3 in July, which was 295B, 21B active, 256,000 context, 598GB. I recently started using model chat templates to better understand their capabilities. Here's Hy4's chat_template.jinja on Hugging Face, which includes this section: {% - if not reasoning_effort is defined %} {% - set reasoning_effort = 'high' %} {% - elif reasoning_effort not in [ 'high' , 'no_think' ] %} {% - if reasoning_effort is none %} {{- raise_exception('reasoning_effort error : None, should be no_think/high') }} {% - else %} {{- raise_exception('reasoning_effort error : ' + reasoning_effort + ', should be no_think/high') }} {% - endif %} {% - endif %} So it looks like there are just two reasoning effort levels: "high" (the default) and "no_think" (reason by disabled). items.title: Understanding ChatGPT Work
items.summary: OpenAI announced ChatGPT Work on July 9th, and have been furiously iterating on it ever since. It is an extraordinarily confusing and very powerful product. Here's what I've figured out about it so far. ChatGPT Work is actually two products The more interesting version of ChatGPT Work is the one that runs in the cloud. This can be accessed via chatgpt.com or through the ChatGPT mobile apps. Let's call it Work Cloud . If you install the ChatGPT desktop app - the app that used to be called Codex - you gain access to a thing called ChatGPT Work that can access files and run programs directly on your computer. Let's call that one Work Local . This one feels more like regular Codex re-skinned to be less intimidating to non-software-developers. ( Update : Work Cloud is also available from the ChatGPT desktop app, via a Where should this chat run? dropdown.) For the rest of this article I'm going to talk exclusively about Work Cloud. Work is for paid subscribers only Right now, ChatGPT Work (in both flavors) is available only to $20/month and up subscribers. Free users and $8/month Go users do not have access. Work has features that aren't available in Chat The interface for accessing Work is a tab selector, which presents it as an alternative to Chat: The obvious question is when should I use Chat, and when should I use Work? OpenAI's official answer to that question is: Use Chat when you want an answer, explanation, brainstorm, or short draft. items.title: Introducing wrapture
items.summary: Introducing wrapture New from Graham Dumpleton (of wrapt , mod_wsgi, and New Relic's Python agent fame), who describes Wrapture as taking the monkeypatching ideas from wrapt and extending them to apply to testing and tracing at the same time. Wrapture ( full documentation here ) makes it easy to wrap any function or method such that all access can be traced, or can be overridden to return a different value. It acts as both an alternative to unittest.mock and a way to implement tracing against an existing project: Attaching observation to code you do not control, recording what flows through it, and doing so without disturbing the program being watched, is a problem I have never really stopped thinking about. Wrapture includes OpenTelemetry support and even has an entirely configuration-based mechanism for adding tracing to an existing Python project, which looks like this: capture = " summary " [[ observe ]] target = " domain:Calculator " name = [ " outer " , " inner " ] [[ sink ]] type = " jsonlines " path = " trace.jsonl " This is still a very young project - just a few weeks old - but it's off to a very promising start. Interestingly, this is also Graham's first attempt at large entirely agent-driven project: Every line of code and documentation in wrapture was written by an AI assistant working under my direction. I want to be upfront about that, and equally upfront about what it was not. items.title: Amazon Cognito 新增用于重置用户 TOTP 配置的管理员 API 操作
items.summary: Amazon Cognito 现提供一个新的管理员 API 操作，用于重置用户的基于时间的一次性密码（TOTP）多重身份验证（MFA）配置。当用户无法访问其 TOTP 设备时，管理员可以移除该设备关联，允许用户在下一次登录时注册新设备。 这样一来，当用户无法访问其 TOTP 设备时，管理员无需重新创建账户即可恢复被锁定的用户。客户可以在维持 MFA 强制要求的同时提供恢复路径。 这项新功能已在提供 Amazon Cognito 的所有 AWS 区域 推出。要开始使用该功能，请使用 AWS CLI、SDK 或 API 访问 AdminDeleteSoftwareToken API。请参阅 开发人员指南 ，获取相关说明。

items.title: Amazon Connect Customer 现支持座席排班中的非计划性缩编
items.summary: Amazon Connect Customer 现支持管理人员在座席排班中输入非计划性缩编，从而在出现座席非计划性缺勤（如迟到登录或非计划性病假）时提供更准确的人员配置情况。管理人员可以将非计划性缩编假设直接上传到座席排班中，并立即查看更新的排班指标，如计划在岗人数、净人员配置和预测服务级别——每项指标均根据非计划性缩编进行调整。例如，如果下周一上午 8 点排班工作的座席中有 10% 预计因迟到登录而无法到岗，在考虑非计划性缩编后，预测服务级别将从 90% 降至 85%。该功能使劳动力管理人员能够主动应对因座席非计划性不可用而可能产生的人员配置缺口，从而提高排班准确性，并增强其维持目标服务级别的能力。 这项功能已在提供 Amazon Connect Customer 座席排班功能的所有 AWS 区域 推出。要了解有关 Amazon Connect Customer 座席排班功能的更多信息，请单击 此处 。

items.title: 适用于 Amazon S3 的 Mountpoint 新增内存使用控制功能
items.summary: 适用于 Amazon S3 的 Mountpoint 现在可以限制内存使用量，可以根据其运行环境自动限制，也可以按照您的定义进行限制。这样一来，您可以将 Mountpoint 与内存密集型应用一同运行，例如在多个应用共享同一内存预算的机器学习训练或分析工作负载中。 此前，Mountpoint 的内存使用量可能随着时间推移，根据使用模式而扩展，因此在与其它内存密集型应用竞争时可能导致性能或稳定性问题。通过此次发布，您可以为 Mountpoint 定义内存目标，以便为您的应用预留内存。或者，Mountpoint 可以根据其运行环境自动确定安全默认值。例如，在 Amazon EKS 中运行时，Mountpoint 可以自动检测容器的指定内存预算。在内存压力下，Mountpoint 会减慢操作速度以保持在此预算范围内，从而使您能够在具有严格内存分配的容器中运行 Mountpoint。 Mountpoint 在所有 AWS 区域均可用。要升级到最新版本，请访问 Mountpoint GitHub 存储库 。要了解有关 Mountpoint 的更多信息，请参阅 Mountpoint GitHub 存储库中的 概述页面 和 配置指南 。

items.title: Amazon Connect Customer 现支持在绩效评估中进行分值计分
items.summary: Amazon Connect Customer 现支持使用分值计分来评估人工代理和人工智能代理的绩效，为管理人员在配置评估分数方面提供更大的灵活性。通过分值计分，管理人员根据每个标准对业务的重要程度为其分配分值，最终得分为所得分值之和。相比之下，在现有的百分比计分方式中，每个问题被分配权重，且权重需合计至 100%。例如，一次分值评估可能为解决客户问题奖励 40 分，为满足合规要求奖励 20 分，为恰当的问候语奖励 10 分——无需各项得分合计为 100。管理人员控制分值授予方式：将多项合规标准合并为一个多项选择题以缩短表单，将通话原因排除在评分之外，或为良好的客户关系给予额外加分。管理人员决定哪些因素计入评分、各因素权重多少，以及哪些表现可获得额外加分，从而使分数反映业务最为重视的内容。 此功能已在提供 Amazon Connect Customer 的所有区域推出。要了解更多信息，请参阅我们的 文档 和 网页 。

items.title: AWS Backup 现已在九个新增 AWS 区域支持 Amazon DocumentDB 的跨区域备份复制和逻辑上受物理隔离的保管库
items.summary: AWS Backup 现已在以下九个新增 AWS 区域支持跨 AWS 区域复制 Amazon DocumentDB 备份并将其存储在逻辑上受物理隔离的保管库中：亚太地区（香港、雅加达、墨尔本、大阪）、欧洲地区（西班牙、斯德哥尔摩、苏黎世）、非洲（开普敦）和以色列（特拉维夫）。 随着跨区域复制在上述区域的推出，您可以使用备份计划或按需复制作业，将 DocumentDB 备份复制进和复制出这些区域。这有助于您满足灾难恢复、业务连续性和合规性要求。您还可以将 DocumentDB 备份复制到这些区域中的逻辑上受物理隔离的保管库，以存储不可变且隔离的备份，这些备份默认处于锁定状态，并使用 AWS 自有或客户托管的密钥进行加密。使用 AWS Resource Access Manager（RAM）共享保管库以进行恢复，并通过多方审批在账户遭到入侵时保护保管库的访问安全，从而缩短数据丢失事件的恢复时间。 要开始使用，请访问 AWS Backup 控制台、AWS 命令行界面（CLI）或 AWS SDK。有关受支持的区域和功能的完整列表，请访问 AWS Backup 文档 。要了解有关逻辑上受物理隔离的保管库的更多信息，请参阅 产品页面 和 定价页面 。

items.title: Amazon EC2 R8id 实例现已在更多 AWS 区域推出
items.summary: Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud（Amazon EC2）R8id 实例现已在更多区域推出。R8id 实例现已在亚太地区（孟买、马来西亚、悉尼）、加拿大（中部），以及欧洲地区（爱尔兰、斯德哥尔摩）推出。 R8id 实例配备高达 22.8TB 的 NVMe SSD 本地实例存储，是 R6id 的 3 倍，并提供高达 3.3 倍的内存带宽，与 R6id 实例相比性能提升高达 43%。这些实例非常适合内存密集型工作负载，可充分发挥高性能本地存储优势，适用场景包括内存数据库、实时大数据分析、大型内存缓存和数据处理应用。 此外，客户现在可以使用 EC2 实例带宽权重配置将这些实例的网络和 Amazon EBS 带宽调整 25%，以便更灵活地分配带宽资源，从而更好地优化工作负载。这些实例就 24xlarge、48xlarge、metal-24xl 和 metal-48xl 大小提供 Elastic Fabric Adapter (EFA) 网络。 客户可以通过节省计划、按需型实例和竞价型实例购买这些实例。有关更多信息，请访问 Amazon EC2 R8id 页面 。

items.title: Amazon EC2 C8id 和 M8id 实例现已在更多 AWS 区域推出
items.summary: 具有高达 22.8TB 基于 NVMe 的本地 SSD 块级存储的 Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud（Amazon EC2）C8id 和 M8id 实例现已在更多区域推出。C8id 实例现已在亚太地区（悉尼）和加拿大（中部）推出，M8id 实例现已在亚太地区（孟买）和加拿大（中部）推出。 与之前的第六代实例相比，Amazon EC2 C8id 和 M8id 实例提供 3 倍的 vCPU、内存和本地存储。与之前的第六代 C6id 和 M6id 实例相比，这些实例的计算性能提升多达 43%，内存带宽增加了 3.3 倍。与之前的第六代实例相比，这些实例处理 I/O 密集型数据库工作负载的性能可提高最多 46%，在 I/O 密集型实时数据分析中，查询速度可提高最多 30%。 C8id 实例 非常适合计算密集型工作负载，包括需要访问高速、低延迟本地存储的工作负载，例如视频编码、图像处理和其他形式的媒体处理。 M8id 实例 非常适合需要平衡计算和内存资源，以及高速、低延迟的本地数据块存储（包括数据日志记录、媒体处理和中等规模数据存储）的工作负载。 此外，客户现在可以使用 EC2 实例带宽权重配置将这些实例的网络和 Amazon EBS 带宽调整 25%，以便更灵活地分配带宽资源，从而更好地优化工作负载。这些实例就 24xlarge、48xlarge、metal-24xl 和 metal-48xl 大小提供 Elastic Fabric Adapter (EFA) 网络。 客户可以通过节省计划、按需型实例和竞价型实例购买这些实例。有关更多信息，请访问 Amazon EC2 C8id 和 Amazon EC2 M8id 页面。

items.title: Amazon EC2 M8i 和 M8i-flex 实例现已在加拿大西部（卡尔加里）区域推出
items.summary: 自今日起，Amazon EC2 M8i 和 M8i-flex 实例已在加拿大西部（卡尔加里）区域推出。这些实例由定制英特尔至强 6 处理器提供支持，仅在 AWS 上可用，在云中的同类英特尔处理器中性能最高，内存带宽最快。与上一代基于英特尔的实例相比，M8i 和 M8i-flex 实例的性价比提升了高达 15%，内存带宽增加了 2.5 倍。其性能较 M7i 和 M7i-flex 实例提升了高达 20%，特定工作负载下的性能提升甚至更为显著。与 M7i 和 M7i-flex 实例相比，M8i 和 M8i-flex 实例在运行 PostgreSQL 数据库时速度提升了高达 30%，在运行 NGINX Web 应用程序时速度提升了高达 60%，在运行 AI 深度学习推荐模型时速度提升了高达 40%。 M8i-flex 实例是大多数通用型工作负载（如 Web 服务器、应用程序服务器、微服务、中小型数据存储、虚拟桌面和企业应用程序）实现性价比优势的最简单方法。R8i-flex 实例提供最常见的大小，从 large 到 16xlarge。对于没有充分利用所有计算资源的应用程序来说，这是不错的首选。 M8i 实例是所有通用型工作负载的理想选择，尤其适用于需要最大实例大小或持续高 CPU 使用率的工作负载。经过 SAP 认证的 M8i 实例提供 13 种大小，包括 2 种裸机大小以及适用于超大型应用程序的全新 96xlarge 大小。 要开始使用，请登录 AWS 管理控制台 。有关新实例的更多信息，请访问 M8i 和 M8i-flex 实例页面 ，或参阅 AWS 新闻 博客 。

items.title: Amazon GameLift Servers 增强型 DDoS 防护现已推出
items.summary: Amazon GameLift Servers 现提供增强型 DDoS 防护，这是一项新的防护层，可在无需任何配置的情况下保护游戏服务器免受常见的网络层和传输层 DDoS 攻击。 从您在 Amazon GameLift Servers 上启动游戏服务器的那一刻起，增强型 DDoS 防护即已生效，无需启用或选择加入。 增强型 DDoS 防护提供主动式、针对游戏优化的流量整形缓解措施，这些措施基于 AWS 在保护全球部分规模最大的游戏过程中积累的经验进行调优，可防御第 3 层和第 4 层的常见流量型攻击，包括 UDP 反射攻击、SYN 泛洪攻击及其他常见的 DDoS 攻击向量。这建立在 AWS Shield Standard 为所有 AWS 服务提供的基准网络级防护之上。对于需要更强防护以抵御复杂或有针对性的攻击的游戏，Amazon GameLift Servers Player Gateway 通过基于中继的网络架构提供最高级别的 DDoS 防御。这些防护层协同工作，当您启用 Player Gateway 后，您的队列除了获得基于中继的防护之外，还将继续受益于增强型 DDoS 防护的流量整形功能。 增强型 DDoS 防护面向 Amazon GameLift Servers 客户提供，无额外费用。适用于所有受支持的 Amazon GameLift Servers 区域，但中国（北京）和中国（宁夏）区域除外，该功能适用于使用 Amazon GameLift Servers Server SDK 5（SDKv5）的队列。有关更多信息，请参阅 Amazon GameLift Servers 文档 。

items.title: AWS Glue 现已在 AWS GovCloud（美国）区域支持远程 Apache Iceberg 目录的目录联合身份验证
items.summary: AWS Glue 现已在 AWS GovCloud（美国）区域支持远程 Iceberg REST 目录的目录联合身份验证。这项功能支持使用 AWS 分析引擎直接、安全地访问存储在 Amazon S3 中并在远程目录中编目的 Iceberg 表。 借助目录联合身份验证功能，您可以使用首选的 AWS 分析引擎联合到远程目录中的 Iceberg 表，无需移动或复制表。当数据团队查询 Iceberg 表时，它会在 AWS Glue Data Catalog 与远程目录之间实时同步元数据，确保查询结果始终基于最新的元数据。现在，在使用首选的 AWS 分析引擎分析远程 Iceberg 表时，您可以为工作负载选择最优的性价比方案，并在数据发现或查询过程中保持一致的安全控制。目录联合身份验证功能支持多种分析引擎，包括 Amazon Redshift、Amazon EMR、Amazon Athena、AWS Glue，以及 Apache Spark 等第三方引擎。 目录联合身份验证功能使用 AWS Lake Formation 进行访问控制，让您在与其他数据使用者共享远程目录表时，能够使用精细访问控制、跨账户共享和可信身份传播。这项功能可以与支持 Iceberg REST 规范的目录实现进行集成。 您可以通过 Lake Formation 控制台、AWS Glue 和 Lake Formation 的 SDK 和 API 使用目录联合身份验证。该功能已在 AWS GovCloud（美国东部）和 AWS GovCloud（美国西部）区域全面推出。要了解更多信息，请访问 文档 。
